model_answer:
## Short answer

Lemonade **beat or hit every line** of the full-year 2024 guidance it issued with Q3 2024 results (Oct 30, 2024) — and it beat the *original* February 2024 guidance by an even wider margin. Management characterized 2024 as delivering on guidance "with notable precision." The two headline metrics (IFP growth and Adjusted EBITDA loss) landed at or better than the favorable end of the range.

## The comparison

Guidance given in the **Q3 2024 shareholder letter / Oct. 30, 2024 call** vs. **FY2024 actuals reported Feb. 26, 2025**:

| FY2024 metric | Guidance (set with Q3'24) | FY2024 actual | vs. guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-force premium (IFP) | $940M – $944M | **$943.7M** | In range; top end (+26% YoY) |
| Gross earned premium | $823M – $826M | **$827.3M** | Beat high end by ~$1.3M |
| Revenue | $522M – $524M | **$526.5M** | Beat high end by ~$2.5M |
| Adjusted EBITDA loss | ($155M) – ($151M) | **($149.7M)** | Beat — $1.3M better than best end |
| Stock-based comp | ~$64M | **$64.5M** | In line |
| Capital expenditures | ~$10M | **$9.4M** | Slightly under |
| Weighted avg. shares | ~71M | **71.0M** | In line |

**Scorecard:** 3 beats (GEP, revenue, Adj. EBITDA), 3 essentially in line (IFP, SBC, share count), 1 modestly under (capex — a favorable outcome).

## Context worth noting

- **Versus the original plan:** In February 2024 Lemonade guided IFP of $938–942M and an Adj. EBITDA loss of ($160)–($155)M. So the final $943.7M IFP came in *above* that original range's top, and the ($149.7M) EBITDA loss was ~$5M better than the best end of the original guide. Along the way (Q3) they raised GEP and revenue guidance while reaffirming the rest.
- **Q4 itself also beat its own guide:** GEP $226.4M vs. $222–225M, revenue $148.8M vs. $144–146M, and Adj. EBITDA loss ($23.8M) vs. the guided ($29M)–($25M).
- **The beat was quality-driven, not one-off:** gross profit nearly doubled to $166.9M (+98% YoY) with gross margin expanding to 32% from 20%; TTM gross loss ratio improved 12 points to 73% (inside the target range); net loss narrowed 15% to $202.2M; and FY2024 Adj. FCF was **+$48M**, the company's first full year of positive adjusted free cash flow. Growth spend more than doubled ($55M → $122M) while expenses ex-growth-spend rose only 2%.
- **Caveat on the "in line" IFP:** the Q3 guidance had already been set after Lemonade flagged the deliberate non-renewal of ~$25M of homeowners IFP in 2H'24 for underwriting reasons, so hitting the range reflected both organic growth and that planned shrinkage. IFP growth accelerated for a fifth straight quarter (26%).
- **One soft spot:** annual dollar retention slipped 1 point to 86%, tied to those underwriting-driven non-renewals.

Note: some secondary outlets mis-reported the 2025 guidance figures ($938–942M / ($160)–($155)M) as 2025 numbers — those were actually the *original February 2024* FY2024 targets. The actual FY2025 guide set in Feb. 2025 was IFP of $1.203–1.208B and an Adj. EBITDA loss of ($140)–($135)M, including a ~$20M hit from the California wildfires.
